clue.text: One’s pencilled in as reserve to go by second vessel

indicators.note: to go by means to be placed beside, so the reserve word sits after the other pieces

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for second
a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat
to reserve a table or seat is to book it

explanation.surface: A substitute player is pencilled in as reserve and must travel on a second boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pencilled in' suggests a provisional booking, but literally it is where an artist does pencil drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's pad of blank pages is something a person draws in with pencil, so it is one that is pencilled in.

clue.text: Heard cracks when cycling and turned round

indicators.note: cycling moves the final letter round to the front of the word, like a wheel turning one notch

blocks.note: cracks are jokes, and jokes that play on sound are heard as puns

explanation.surface: Someone hears cracking noises from a bike and turns round to look.
explanation.walkthrough: PUNS with its last letter brought to the front gives SPUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Spun is the past tense of spin, meaning rotated or whirled about.

clue.text: Keeps secret chapter and verse to undermine opponents

indicators.note: in a down clue, to undermine something is to sit underneath it, so these pieces come lower

blocks.note: East and North are opposing partnerships at the bridge table
C is the abbreviation for chapter
joins the two pieces
odes are lyric poems, so verse

explanation.surface: A spy hunts out scripture references to sabotage rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chapter and verse' reads as a set phrase for exact detail, but it splits into two pieces. Bridge players sit as North, South, East and West, with East and North on opposite sides.
explanation.definitionFit: To encode a message is to turn it into cipher so that its content stays hidden from outsiders.

clue.text: Revolutionary sadder about eating the same English food

indicators.note: about in the sense of all around, scattered, tells us the letters are disordered
something eating takes other material inside itself

blocks.note: Che Guevara is the crossword's favourite revolutionary
taken as written
the same word as the revolutionary just used, Guevara's first name again
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A gloomy revolutionary sits brooding over a plate of English grub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The same' is a clever repeat: it stands for CHE a second time, so CHE plus E goes inside the rearranged SADDER, after the first CHE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheddar is a hard cheese from Somerset, eaten throughout the world as a staple dairy foodstuff.

clue.text: Marine plant — reptile with three feet swallowing tons

indicators.note: swallowing takes something inside, so the pieces either side enclose the extra letter

blocks.note: a boa is a large constricting snake
a yard measures three feet
T is the abbreviation for tons

explanation.surface: A sea plant is pictured as a snake a yard long gulping down weights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marine plant' looks like seaweed, but plant here means an industrial works.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant can be a works or factory, and a yard where vessels are built and repaired is such a seaside works.

clue.text: Published work showing eclipse

blocks.note: a book that is out has been published
to do a job is to work at it

explanation.surface: A published scientific paper about an eclipse.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse a rival is to surpass them, putting their achievement in the shade.

clue.text: A buzz about Scandinavian record

indicators.note: about means turned around, so the pieces read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
a gas is informal for something thrilling or fun, a buzz

explanation.surface: Excitement surrounds a Swedish chart-topping disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagas are medieval Norse and Icelandic prose narratives chronicling heroes and families.

clue.text: Botched data read upside down, oddly lacking style

indicators.note: lacking the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even-placed ones
in a down entry, turning things upside down reads them from bottom to top

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth letters and so on of these three words

explanation.surface: Garbled information has been read the wrong way up, oddly without flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Botched' looks like an anagram signal, but it is part of the letter source; keep the even letters, then reverse them.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Deco is the geometric decorative design movement of the 1920s and 1930s.

clue.text: Evaluation of idiots on street collecting team

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it
collecting means gathering in, so one piece holds another inside it

blocks.note: asses are fools
St is the abbreviation for street
a team is a body of men, as in a side of men

explanation.surface: A scout files a report on fools out in the road gathering a squad.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a judgement of worth or quality, a formal appraisal.

clue.text: Relation seen in sordid article ostracised

indicators.note: someone ostracised is shut out, so that word is removed

blocks.note: sordid means dirty
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A family member turns up in a seedy tabloid story and is shunned.
explanation.walkthrough: Take AN from the end of UNCLEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A relation is any kinsman, and a parent's brother is one such family member.

clue.text: Opposed to party faction’s twisted solutions

indicators.note: twisted round, the word is turned to face the other way

blocks.note: anti means against
a do is a party
a set is a clique or group

explanation.surface: A political group's warped policies oppose the party line.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s means 'is': the faction is twisted.
explanation.definitionFit: Antidotes are remedies that counteract poison, so cures or answers to a problem.

clue.text: Maybe setter’s tight after time off — it’s a mess

indicators.note: after places one piece behind the other in the order

blocks.note: a setter is a breed of gun dog, so a setter's is a dog's; Maybe marks the example
a break is time off work
held fast means held tight

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler got drunk on a day off and now everything is chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Setter' and 'tight' (drunk) paint a tipsy compiler, but the setter is a dog and tight means firmly fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: Dog's breakfast is an informal British idiom for a muddle or botched job.

clue.text: Pine props put down by old man, wiggly things

indicators.note: put down by means set beside, so this pair follows the other piece

blocks.note: old man is slang for father
to pine for is to long for
legs are supports

explanation.surface: Father sets down supports made of pine timber, which wobble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pine' looks like wood, but it is the verb meaning yearn.
explanation.definitionFit: Crane flies with their thin dangling limbs wriggle and wobble about; they are the British name for these insects.

clue.text: Sense head will go on strike — there’s much swearing here

indicators.note: in a down clue, going on something means sitting above it

blocks.note: wit means good sense
a ness is a headland
to box is to punch

explanation.surface: A sensible boss will join a walkout, and there's plenty of cursing about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Swearing suggests foul language, but here it is swearing an oath to tell the truth.
explanation.definitionFit: In a court, witnesses take the oath in the stand before giving evidence, so oaths are sworn there constantly.

clue.text: They cover river when sunrise breaks across it

indicators.note: something that breaks falls apart, so its letters scatter into a new order
across it means stretched over the other piece, enclosing it

blocks.note: taken as written
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Mist blankets the river as dawn breaks over it.
explanation.definitionFit: Insurance companies provide cover against loss, a policy protecting the holder.

clue.text: Out of a black tower

blocks.note: taken as written
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
to loom is to tower over

explanation.surface: Someone escapes from a dark tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tower' looks like a noun, a building, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Flowers that are out have opened their petals, which is what blossoming means.

clue.text: Jumbo seen in show with an act that’s often repeated

blocks.note: a gig is a live performance
taken as written
a tic is a habitual twitch or mannerism

explanation.surface: An elephant appears at a circus doing the same trick over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: Jumbo suggests the famous circus elephant, but here it is an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumbo as an adjective means very large, huge, enormous.

clue.text: Speed brought in by city’s divine females

indicators.note: brought in by means carried inside, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: NY is New York, plus the possessive S
miles per hour measures speed

explanation.surface: A city's goddesses bring in rapid change.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology these are minor goddesses of nature, spirits of rivers and woods.

clue.text: Troops crossing strait — I limped over

indicators.note: crossing means spanning the gap between words, so the letters run across them
turned over, the letters read the other way

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling these words

explanation.surface: Soldiers cross a narrow sea channel and a wounded one limps across.
explanation.definitionFit: A militia is a body of citizen soldiers raised as a reserve force.

clue.text: Rotten row EMI timidly rejected, partly being out of date

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the letters read in the opposite direction
partly means only part of these words is used, a run inside them

blocks.note: the run of letters straddling these words

explanation.surface: A record label shyly turns down a terrible quarrel, as it seems old hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something worn by long use or age is stale, hackneyed and old-fashioned.

clue.text: East German with megabucks — this one has some neck

blocks.note: Ost is the German word for east
someone with millions is wealthy

explanation.surface: A wealthy man from East Germany shows plenty of cheek.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has some neck' sounds like having a nerve; literally the bird has a very long neck.
explanation.definitionFit: This large flightless African bird is famous for its long bare neck.

clue.text: When prices jump or vault, it’s said makers will be twitchy and tense

indicators.note: it's said tells us to take the sound of the preceding word, not its spelling
something twitchy jerks about, so its letters are jumbled

blocks.note: a vault is an underground storeroom; one who sells sounds the same
taken as written
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: With prices leaping and vaulting, manufacturers are said to be nervous and on edge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jump or vault' look like a pair of synonyms, but vault is a storeroom and starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: When demand outstrips supply, vendors can raise prices, so costs rise sharply in such conditions.

clue.text: Fine to sound like Bono?

indicators.note: to sound like says the answer is pronounced like the name that follows

blocks.note: Sonny Bono was the singer of the 1960s duo Sonny and Cher

explanation.surface: Is it fine to sound like the U2 singer?
explanation.walkthrough: Bono suggests the U2 frontman, but the Bono wanted is Sonny Bono, Cher's former partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine weather is clear and bright, with the sun shining.

clue.text: Leader’s talent’s giving second half priority

indicators.note: giving the second half priority puts the back two letters before the front two

blocks.note: art is talent or skill, and the possessive adds S

explanation.surface: A boss's flair lets the second-in-command take precedence.
explanation.walkthrough: ARTS becomes TS plus AR.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsar was the emperor of Russia, so a supreme ruler; the word also means a powerful official.

clue.text: Goat fruitcake? It could be edible

blocks.note: a goat is a butter, an animal that butts
fruitcake and nut are both slang for a crazy person

explanation.surface: Could a fruitcake made with goat be fit to eat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruitcake' looks like the dish, but it is slang for a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American walnut tree and its oily seed, which can be eaten; also a squash variety.

clue.text: A crew from the East also called

indicators.note: reading from the east in an across entry means going right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
to crew a boat is to sail it

explanation.surface: A boat team from the Orient also has a name.
explanation.definitionFit: Alias is used before a second name, meaning otherwise known as.

clue.text: Cross-beam in medical facility

blocks.note: X is a cross
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: A crossbeam supports a hospital building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross-beam' reads as a building timber, but the hyphen hides two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals have a radiography department where patients are imaged with radiation.

clue.text: The old retiring teacher sadly consuming cold dish

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing backwards, so the letters read in reverse
sadly suggests something gone wrong, so the letters are disarranged
consuming means taking inside, so one letter goes within the others

blocks.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: An elderly teacher about to retire gloomily eats a plate of cold food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold dish' suggests food served chilled, but dish is slang for an attractive person.
explanation.definitionFit: Dish is informal for a good-looking person, someone who draws admiring glances.
